title: agent-shell 0.73 updates

content_html:
August 15, 2026

Another month, another agent-shell update. If you missed the last one, have a look at the 0.63 update. While this post showcases the latest highlights, the full list of changes is far chunkier than what we'll cover.

What's agent-shell?

agent-shell is a native Emacs mode to interact with AI agents powered by ACP (Agent Client Protocol).

agent-shell enters the chat

Since inception in September last year (yikes nearly a year), agent-shell has featured a shell-like experience, powered by comint mode. There's also viewport mode (via agent-shell-prefer-viewport-interaction), if you prefer a more focused experience, and now we have chat mode.

Chat mode fuses comint mode with a more traditional chat-like labelling experience.

We're living on the edge here, so chat mode is now enabled by default. Ok not really that edgy, it's fairly safe (powered overlays) and can be disabled entirely via (setq agent-shell-chat-mode-enabled nil). Chat mode itself is a minor mode, so you can always toggle it on and off via M-x agent-shell-chat-mode.

A little more chatter

In the last post, we talked about making agent-shell less chatty with more grouping for the likes of tool calls and agent thinking, all collapsed by default. If that's far too quiet, you can expand by default via (setq agent-shell-activity-group-expand-by-default t). If you found these two settings either too quiet or too chatty, we now have a third alternative via (setq agent-shell-activity-group-expand-by-default 'latest). When set, only the latest grouped activity is expanded by default, and automatically collapsed when the agent moves on to something else.

I've become quite fond of this feature (thank you @nhojb for the PR), so yes. It's also enabled by default.

Prompt queueing

Queuing received some improvements. The related commands have been consolidated under agent-shell-prompt-queue.el. You can queue prompts while the agent is busy, then view, resume, or drop pending prompts via M-x agent-shell-prompt-queue, M-x agent-shell-prompt-queue-resume, and M-x agent-shell-prompt-queue-remove. The pending queue is now shown after each new submission.

Compose from anywhere

M-x agent-shell-prompt-compose opens a dedicated buffer for crafting a prompt, and it's now more independent of the shell. You can invoke it from any buffer (it resolves to the right shell), C-c C-c sends and returns you to whatever you were doing (fire and forget), and C-u C-c C-c submits the prompt and immediately lets you craft another queued prompt.

Start typing sooner

Shell initialization may take a second or two, depending on what agent you're using, which meant you had to wait for initialization before you could start typing into your new shell. Unnecessary, so that's no longer the case. Shell prompts are now offered as soon as possible, so one can get typing.

Markdown lists

While Markdown lists are easily digestible without special rendering, we can do better than that, so we now give them a better treatment with normalized padding, indentation, and of course, civilized bullets.

TAB navigation improvements + hints

TAB navigation made it into agent-shell fairly early on. I love being able to TAB my way into any section in the buffer and press RET to toggle folding. That's great and all, but we can make the navigation experience richer by welcoming the likes of Markdown source blocks, links, and images to the navigation party. Why these in particular? They are all actionable by RET too, of course.

While you'd rightly assume RET opens links to local text files in Emacs and delegates to browsers when needed, Markdown source blocks and images get a similar treatment. While their respective RET actions may not be as obvious, we can certainly make them much more discoverable, so we now add hints. Landing point on an actionable item now echoes a hint of what you can do and which key does it (say, "Press RET to copy" on a source block, "Press + to enlarge" on an image, and so on). Hints are also shown on mouse over events.

Image size hints

While agent-shell offers agent-shell-markdown-image-max-width for customizing image sizes, it's fairly restrictive. Not all images are the same, so why force them all to fit within the same constraint? agent-shell-markdown-image-max-width continues to offer a preferred default, but you can now scale images differently by getting the agent to annotate Markdown images with Pandoc-style link attributes.

The attribute block goes right after the image, taking a width and/or height in pixels or percentages:

![alt](image.png){width=300}
![alt](image.png){width=50% height=200}

Auto resize

I may be sweating the small stuff here, but this was really grinding my gears. We have lovely Markdown table rendering, which I'm glad we do as LLMs aren't always great at producing perfectly aligned tables. In the best of cases, the LLMs align the table perfectly, but it's just too wide for our Emacs window. Luckily, our lovely rendering also wraps cells to make them fit into our window. The thing is, all that lovely rendering goes out the door the moment you either resize your Emacs frame or merely split your window, resulting in a monstrosity like this:

I know. I'm sweating the small stuff here, but hey we don't have to live like this. Emacs has all the hooks in the world, so let's track window changes and rejoin the civilized world.

On a much smaller scale, I also wanted auto resize for images, so here you have it…

Manual resize

While we can influence image size at render time, this can still generate undesirable image dimensions, so we can now rescale all images in buffer on demand.

Sometimes a hammer really isn't the right tool, so we can now also rescale an image at point.

Open file links as you please

Opening a local file (from a link, image, or @file mention) now routes through agent-shell-file-display-action, a standard display-buffer action you can customize. The default reuses a window already showing the file, or takes over the current one.

If you'd like a different window arrangement, you could do something like:

(setq agent-shell-file-display-action
      '(display-buffer-pop-up-window))

Xref support

Following a local file link now pushes your origin onto xref's marker stack, so xref-go-back (M-,) brings you right back to where you were in your agent-shell, just like other Emacs jumps.

Use your favorite folding key binding

Foldable fragments now use agent-shell-ui-fragment-map and bind agent-shell-ui-toggle-fragment. If you're not a fan of the RET binding to toggle folding, you can now use your preferred binding.

If TAB is your jam, you can do something like:

(with-eval-after-load 'agent-shell-ui
  (define-key agent-shell-ui-fragment-map
              (kbd "TAB") #'agent-shell-ui-toggle-fragment))

Styling thoughts

If you prefer styling agent thoughts differently, a new agent-shell-thought-body face lets you do just that.

Streaming performance

Streaming performance also received some love. Thanks to @suhail-singh for the profiling and improvements, and to @Scott-Guest and @claytharrison for the trace analysis and benchmarking in #757.

Richer display of options

The "Available config options" section now displays possible values.

Public functions

Dynamic agent configs

agent-shell-agent-configs can now be set to a function, letting you compute the available agent configurations dynamically rather than hard-coding a static list. The function is called on every access, so it stays current across code reloads.

Maybe you'd like to list only available agents. Here's a rough snippet.

(setq agent-shell-agent-configs
      (lambda ()
        (seq-filter
         (lambda (maker)
           (when-let* ((client (ignore-errors
                                 (funcall (map-elt (funcall maker) :client-maker)
                                          (current-buffer))))
                       (command (map-elt client :command)))
             (executable-find command)))
         (agent-shell-default-agent-config-makers))))

Subscribe to agent message chunks

agent-shell-subscribe-to now broadcasts an agent-message-chunk event, handy for external integrations that want to observe streamed output.

Remote agents

executable-find now works correctly on remote hosts (#742 by @CeleritasCelery), smoothing out TRAMP-driven remote agents.

New third-party packages

agent-shell-hq joins the family, offering an interface for managing multiple agent-shell sessions.

Maintenance and housekeeping

If you peeked at the commit logs, you'll notice I've been working daily on agent-shell, keeping up with project inflow. Since last month, 27 issues have been closed and 13 pull requests merged. As of today, the backlog sits at 11 open issues and 5 open PRs (versus 13 and 4 last time around). If there's something you'd like me to prioritize, feel free to ping.

agent-shell needs your support

Vendor-neutral tooling matters more than ever, and there are a couple of ways to help keep agent-shell going. Some cost money, others just a click. All are appreciated ;)

agent-shell is just me, an indie dev, while the tools it competes with have well-funded teams behind them. Time spent on agent-shell is time away from work that pays the bills, so if it's useful to you, please consider sponsoring the project. And if your employer benefits from your agent-shell use, nudge them to chip in too, they can typically contribute at a scale individuals can't.

GitHub stars for exposure

GitHub stars help with exposure, attracting new users and potential sponsors. Starring agent-shell costs nothing and can potentially help bring in more funding, so if you don't mind a couple of clicks, the project can really use another GitHub star.

Pull requests

Thank you to all contributors for these improvements!

  • #730: Queue requests sent during session/push and submit them when it ends (@catern)
  • #737: Add a workaround for goose (@bergmannf)
  • #740: Add a when-active option to agent-shell-activity-group-expand-by-default (@nhojb)
  • #742: Fix executable-find on remote host (@CeleritasCelery)
  • #743: Preserve "claimed" regions when rendering bold / italic / strikethrough (@alberti42)
  • #746: Avoid repeated system-sleep load attempts (@liaowang11)
  • #748: Preserve properties on escaped Markdown punctuation (@Scott-Guest)
  • #752: Guard group member walk against non-advancing block range (@hamza-m-masood)
  • #756: Preserve point during table rendering (@Lenbok)
  • #762: Document viewport workflow (@KarimAziev)
  • #763: Render raw tool output (@mrychlik)
  • #765: Prevent syntax highlighting from delaying other buffers' mode hooks (@Scott-Guest)
  • #766: Refresh viewport header even with nil agent-shell-prefer-viewport-interaction (@catern)

Liking agent-shell? Would like to see it evolve? Consider sponsoring the effort.

blocks.html_en: Shell initialization may take a second or two, depending on what agent you're using, which meant you had to wait for initialization before you could start typing into your new shell. Unnecessary, so that's no longer the case. Shell prompts are now offered as soon as possible, so one can get typing.

sentences.en: Unnecessary, so that's no longer the case.
sentences.zh: 没有必要了，所以不再这样了。

sentences.en: Shell prompts are now offered as soon as possible, so one can get typing.
sentences.zh: 现在会尽快提供 shell 提示，以便用户可以开始输入。

blocks.html_en: Markdown lists

sentences.en: Markdown lists
sentences.zh: 降价列表

blocks.html_en: While Markdown lists are easily digestible without special rendering, we can do better than that, so we now give them a better treatment with normalized padding, indentation, and of course, civilized bullets.

sentences.en: While Markdown lists are easily digestible without special rendering, we can do better than that, so we now give them a better treatment with normalized padding, indentation, and of course, civilized bullets.
sentences.zh: 虽然 Markdown 列表无需特殊渲染即可轻松理解，但我们可以做得更好，因此我们现在通过规范化的填充、缩进，当然还有文明的项目符号，对它们进行更好的处理。

blocks.html_en: TAB navigation improvements + hints

sentences.en: TAB navigation improvements + hints
sentences.zh: TAB 导航改进 + 提示

blocks.html_en: TAB navigation made it into agent-shell fairly early on. I love being able to TAB my way into any section in the buffer and press RET to toggle folding. That's great and all, but we can make the navigation experience richer by welcoming the likes of Markdown source blocks, links, and images to the navigation party. Why these in particular? They are all actionable by RET too, of course.

sentences.en: TAB navigation made it into agent-shell fairly early on.
sentences.zh: TAB 导航很早就进入了代理 shell。

sentences.en: I love being able to TAB my way into any section in the buffer and press RET to toggle folding.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢能够按 TAB 键进入缓冲区中的任何部分，然后按 RET 切换折叠。

sentences.en: That's great and all, but we can make the navigation experience richer by welcoming the likes of Markdown source blocks, links, and images to the navigation party.
sentences.zh: 这固然很棒，但我们可以通过欢迎 Markdown 源代码块、链接和图像之类的内容来使导航体验更加丰富。

sentences.en: Why these in particular?
sentences.zh: 为什么特别是这些？

sentences.en: They are all actionable by RET too, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，它们也都可以通过 RET 来实施。

blocks.html_en: While you'd rightly assume RET opens links to local text files in Emacs and delegates to browsers when needed, Markdown source blocks and images get a similar treatment. While their respective RET actions may not be as obvious, we can certainly make them much more discoverable, so we now add hints. Landing point on an actionable item now echoes a hint of what you can do and which key does it (say, "Press RET to copy" on a source block, "Press + to enlarge" on an image, and so on). Hints are also shown on mouse over events.

sentences.en: While you'd rightly assume RET opens links to local text files in Emacs and delegates to browsers when needed, Markdown source blocks and images get a similar treatment.
sentences.zh: 虽然您正确地认为 RET 在 Emacs 中打开指向本地文本文件的链接并在需要时委托给浏览器，但 Markdown 源代码块和图像得到类似的处理。

sentences.en: While their respective RET actions may not be as obvious, we can certainly make them much more discoverable, so we now add hints.
sentences.zh: 虽然它们各自的 RET 操作可能不那么明显，但我们当然可以使它们更容易被发现，所以我们现在添加提示。

sentences.en: Landing point on an actionable item now echoes a hint of what you can do and which key does it (say, "Press RET to copy" on a source block, "Press + to enlarge" on an image, and so on).
sentences.zh: 现在，可操作项目上的着陆点会提示您可以执行哪些操作以及执行哪个键（例如，在源块上“按 RET 进行复制”，在图像上“按 + 放大”，等等）。

sentences.en: Hints are also shown on mouse over events.
sentences.zh: 鼠标悬停事件也会显示提示。

blocks.html_en: While agent-shell offers agent-shell-markdown-image-max-width for customizing image sizes, it's fairly restrictive. Not all images are the same, so why force them all to fit within the same constraint? agent-shell-markdown-image-max-width continues to offer a preferred default, but you can now scale images differently by getting the agent to annotate Markdown images with Pandoc-style link attributes.

sentences.en: Auto resize

blocks.html_en: I may be sweating the small stuff here, but this was really grinding my gears. We have lovely Markdown table rendering, which I'm glad we do as LLMs aren't always great at producing perfectly aligned tables. In the best of cases, the LLMs align the table perfectly, but it's just too wide for our Emacs window. Luckily, our lovely rendering also wraps cells to make them fit into our window. The thing is, all that lovely rendering goes out the door the moment you either resize your Emacs frame or merely split your window, resulting in a monstrosity like this:

sentences.en: I may be sweating the small stuff here, but this was really grinding my gears.
sentences.zh: 我可能会因为这些小事而出汗，但这真的让我很累。

sentences.en: We have lovely Markdown table rendering, which I'm glad we do as LLMs aren't always great at producing perfectly aligned tables.
sentences.zh: 我们有可爱的 Markdown 表格渲染，我很高兴我们这样做，因为法学硕士并不总是擅长生成完美对齐的表格。

sentences.en: In the best of cases, the LLMs align the table perfectly, but it's just too wide for our Emacs window.
sentences.zh: 在最好的情况下，法学硕士可以完美地对齐表格，但对于我们的 Emacs 窗口来说太宽了。

sentences.en: Luckily, our lovely rendering also wraps cells to make them fit into our window.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，我们可爱的渲染还包裹了单元格，使它们适合我们的窗口。

sentences.en: The thing is, all that lovely rendering goes out the door the moment you either resize your Emacs frame or merely split your window, resulting in a monstrosity like this:

sentences.en: I know.

sentences.zh: Emacs 拥有世界上所有的钩子，所以让我们跟踪窗口变化并重新加入文明世界。

content_html_zh:
August 15, 2026

又一个月，另一个代理外壳更新。 如果您错过了上一篇，请查看 0.63 更新。 虽然这篇文章展示了最新的亮点，但完整的更改列表比我们将要介绍的内容要厚得多。

什么是代理壳？

agent-shell 是一种原生 Emacs 模式，用于与由 ACP（代理客户端协议）支持的 AI 代理进行交互。

agent-shell 进入聊天

自去年 9 月推出以来（哎呀，已经快一年了），agent-shell 提供了类似 shell 的体验，由 comint 模式提供支持。 如果您喜欢更专注的体验，还有视口模式（通过 agent-shell-prefer-viewport-interaction），现在我们有聊天模式。

聊天模式将 comint 模式与更传统的类似聊天的标签体验融合在一起。

我们生活在边缘，所以现在默认启用聊天模式。 好吧，并不是那么急躁，它相当安全（动力覆盖），并且可以通过（setq agent-shell-chat-mode-enabled nil）完全禁用。 聊天模式本身是一种次要模式，因此您始终可以通过 M-x agent-shell-chat-mode 打开和关闭它。

多一点闲聊

在上一篇文章中，我们讨论了通过对工具调用和代理思考等进行更多分组来减少代理外壳的繁琐程度，默认情况下所有这些都已折叠。 如果这太安静了，您可以通过 (setq agent-shell-activity-group-expand-by-default t) 默认扩展。 如果您发现这两个设置太安静或太吵闹，我们现在有第三种选择（setq agent-shell-activity-group-expand-by-default 'latest）。 设置后，默认情况下仅展开最新分组的活动，并在代理移至其他活动时自动折叠。

我已经变得非常喜欢这个功能（感谢@nhojb 的公关），所以是的。 它也是默认启用的。

及时排队

排队得到了一些改进。 相关命令已合并在agent-shell-prompt-queue.el下。 您可以在代理忙时对提示进行排队，然后通过 M-x agent-shell-prompt-queue、M-x agent-shell-prompt-queue-resume 和 M-x agent-shell-prompt-queue-remove 查看、恢复或删除待处理的提示。 现在，每次新提交后都会显示待处理队列。

随时随地撰写

M-x agent-shell-prompt-compose 打开一个专用缓冲区来制作提示，现在它更加独立于 shell。 您可以从任何缓冲区调用它（它解析为正确的 shell），C-c C-c 发送并返回您正在做的任何事情（即发即忘），C-u C-c C-c 提交提示并立即让您制作另一个排队的提示。

尽早开始打字

Shell 初始化可能需要一两秒的时间，具体取决于您使用的代理，这意味着您必须等待初始化才能开始在新 shell 中输入内容。 没有必要了，所以不再这样了。 现在会尽快提供 shell 提示，以便用户可以开始输入。

降价列表

虽然 Markdown 列表无需特殊渲染即可轻松理解，但我们可以做得更好，因此我们现在通过规范化的填充、缩进，当然还有文明的项目符号，对它们进行更好的处理。

TAB 导航改进 + 提示

TAB 导航很早就进入了代理 shell。 我喜欢能够按 TAB 键进入缓冲区中的任何部分，然后按 RET 切换折叠。 这固然很棒，但我们可以通过欢迎 Markdown 源代码块、链接和图像之类的内容来使导航体验更加丰富。 为什么特别是这些？ 当然，它们也都可以通过 RET 来实施。

虽然您正确地认为 RET 在 Emacs 中打开指向本地文本文件的链接并在需要时委托给浏览器，但 Markdown 源代码块和图像得到类似的处理。 虽然它们各自的 RET 操作可能不那么明显，但我们当然可以使它们更容易被发现，所以我们现在添加提示。 现在，可操作项目上的着陆点会提示您可以执行哪些操作以及执行哪个键（例如，在源块上“按 RET 进行复制”，在图像上“按 + 放大”，等等）。 鼠标悬停事件也会显示提示。

图像尺寸提示

虽然 agent-shell 提供了 agent-shell-markdown-image-max-width 来自定义图像大小，但它具有相当的限制性。 并非所有图像都是相同的，那么为什么要强迫它们全部符合相同的约束呢？ agent-shell-markdown-image-max-width 继续提供首选默认值，但您现在可以通过让代理使用 Pandoc 样式链接属性注释 Markdown 图像来以不同方式缩放图像。

属性块位于图像之后，以像素或百分比为单位获取宽度和/或高度：

![alt](image.png){width=300}
![alt](image.png){width=50% height=200}

自动调整大小

我可能会因为这些小事而出汗，但这真的让我很累。 我们有可爱的 Markdown 表格渲染，我很高兴我们这样做，因为法学硕士并不总是擅长生成完美对齐的表格。 在最好的情况下，法学硕士可以完美地对齐表格，但对于我们的 Emacs 窗口来说太宽了。 幸运的是，我们可爱的渲染还包裹了单元格，使它们适合我们的窗口。 问题是，当你调整 Emacs 框架大小或只是分割窗口时，所有可爱的渲染都会消失，导致像这样的怪物：

我知道。 我为这里的小事而烦恼，但是嘿，我们不必这样生活。 Emacs 拥有世界上所有的钩子，所以让我们跟踪窗口变化并重新加入文明世界。

在更小的规模上，我还想要自动调整图像大小，所以这里你有它......

手动调整大小

虽然我们可以在渲染时影响图像大小，但这仍然会生成不需要的图像尺寸，因此我们现在可以根据需要重新缩放缓冲区中的所有图像。

有时锤子确实不是正确的工具，所以我们现在还可以在此时重新缩放图像。

随意打开文件链接

打开本地文件（从链接、图像或@file提及）现在通过agent-shell-file-display-action（您可以自定义的标准显示缓冲区操作）进行路由。 默认情况下会重用已显示该文件的窗口，或接管当前窗口。

如果您想要不同的窗口排列，您可以执行以下操作：

(setq agent-shell-file-display-action
      '(display-buffer-pop-up-window))

外部参照支持

现在，跟随本地文件链接会将您的原点推送到外部引用的标记堆栈上，因此外部引用返回 (M-,) 会带您直接返回到代理 shell 中的位置，就像其他 Emacs 跳转一样。

使用您最喜欢的折叠键绑定

可折叠片段现在使用agent-shell-ui-fragment-map并绑定agent-shell-ui-toggle-fragment。 如果您不喜欢使用 RET 绑定来切换折叠，您现在可以使用您喜欢的绑定。

如果你喜欢 TAB，你可以这样做：

(with-eval-after-load 'agent-shell-ui
  (define-key agent-shell-ui-fragment-map
              (kbd "TAB") #'agent-shell-ui-toggle-fragment))

造型想法

如果您更喜欢造型代理的想法，新的代理-外壳-思想-主体界面可以让您做到这一点。

流媒体性能

流媒体表演也受到了一些人的喜爱。 感谢@suhail-singh 的分析和改进，感谢@Scott-Guest 和@claytharrison 在#757 中的跟踪分析和基准测试。

更丰富的选项展示

“可用配置选项”部分现在显示可能的值。

公共职能

动态代理配置

agent-shell-agent-configs 现在可以设置为一个函数，让您动态计算可用的代理配置，而不是硬编码静态列表。 该函数在每次访问时都会被调用，因此它在代码重新加载时保持最新状态。

也许您只想列出可用的代理。 这是一个粗略的片段。

(setq agent-shell-agent-configs
      (lambda ()
        (seq-filter
         (lambda (maker)
           (when-let* ((client (ignore-errors
                                 (funcall (map-elt (funcall maker) :client-maker)
                                          (current-buffer))))
                       (command (map-elt client :command)))
             (executable-find command)))
         (agent-shell-default-agent-config-makers))))

订阅代理消息块

agent-shell-subscribe-to 现在广播 agent-message-chunk 事件，对于想要观察流输出的外部集成来说很方便。

远程代理

可执行文件查找现在可以在远程主机上正常工作（#742 by @CeleritasCelery），平滑 TRAMP 驱动的远程代理。

新的第三方软件包

agent-shell-hq 加入该系列，提供用于管理多个 agent-shell 会话的界面。

维护和内务管理

如果您查看提交日志，您会发现我每天都在代理 shell 上工作，跟上项目流入。 自上个月以来，已关闭 27 个问题并合并了 13 个拉取请求。 截至今天，积压的问题有 11 个未解决的问题和 5 个未解决的 PR（上次分别为 13 和 4 个）。 如果您希望我优先处理某些事情，请随时 ping。

Agent-Shell 需要您的支持

供应商中立的工具比以往任何时候都更加重要，有几种方法可以帮助保持代理外壳的运行。 有些需要花钱，有些则只需点击一下即可。 所有人都表示赞赏；）

agent-shell 只有我一个独立开发者，而它的竞争工具背后都有资金雄厚的团队。 在代理 shell 上花费的时间是远离支付账单的工作的时间，所以如果它对您有用，请考虑赞助该项目。 如果你的雇主从你的代理壳的使用中受益，推动他们也参与进来，他们通常可以做出个人无法做到的贡献。

GitHub star 曝光

GitHub 明星有助于提高曝光度，吸引新用户和潜在赞助商。 为agent-shell加注星标不需要任何成本，并且可能有助于带来更多资金，因此，如果您不介意点击几下，该项目确实可以使用另一个 GitHub star。
